package_info.why_malicious: This package is a result of a dependency confusion or namesquatting attack specifically targeting the Kraken cryptocurrency exchange. It contains only a package.json file with a preinstall script that exfiltrates sensitive host information (system details, username, hostname) to an external, attacker-controlled domain. There is no legitimate source code or functionality; the package is designed solely for malicious reconnaissance and data exfiltration during installation.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During preinstall, the script executes a shell command that collects system information (output of uname -a, whoami, and hostname), sends this data via HTTP POST to https://www.analytics-google.com/collect, resulting in exfiltration of host reconnaissance data to an external attacker-controlled domain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The preinstall script is configured to run automatically during package installation and sends detailed host information to an external, non-canonical domain. This behavior is highly indicative of malicious reconnaissance and data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages rarely use preinstall scripts, and never to collect and transmit system or user data to unknown or suspicious domains. Preinstall scripts are typically reserved for setup tasks, not for network exfiltration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may collect environment or system information for telemetry, but this is always documented, opt-in, and sent to well-known, trusted domains. Legitimate analytics never occur silently during preinstall without user consent.
key_indicators: preinstall script in package.json making outbound network requests
use of curl to POST system/user/host info to an external domain
external domain (www.analytics-google.com) not associated with legitimate analytics providers
absence of any source code or functional files beyond package.json

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is installed as a result of dependency confusion or typosquatting, typically when an internal build system or developer inadvertently pulls the attacker-controlled package from the public npm registry.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of the malicious preinstall script.

attack_chain.action: The preinstall script executes automatically during the npm install process, collecting system, user, and host information and exfiltrating it to the attacker's external domain.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives detailed host reconnaissance data, enabling further targeted attacks or lateral movement.

behavioral_signatures: preinstall script in package.json that executes network requests
collection and exfiltration of system, user, or host information during package installation
npm packages containing only package.json with no additional source files
file_indicators: package.json with a preinstall script invoking curl or similar network utilities
absence of index.js, main.js, or any other source code files in the package
network_indicators: HTTP POST requests to https://www.analytics-google.com/collect during npm install
presence of suspicious or non-canonical domains in preinstall scripts
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan npm packages for preinstall scripts in package.json that invoke network utilities (e.g., curl, wget) to send data externally, especially those that POST system or user information. Flag packages that lack any source code beyond package.json. Monitor for outbound HTTP requests to domains such as www.analytics-google.com during package installation, and alert on any domains not associated with legitimate analytics or telemetry providers.
